key_insight: A data-driven framework that uses skeleton-based biomechanical analysis and motion modeling can quantify dart-throwing mechanics and deliver personalized, actionable training guidance beyond single-point release metrics.
problem_solved: Existing coaching and quantitative methods focus on local or static metrics and cannot capture whole-body coordination or provide individualized, data-backed training plans for improving dart accuracy and consistency.
method: Capture player motion with skeleton/pose estimation and extract biomechanical features (joint angles, velocities, release timing, coordination metrics).
Build motion models (statistical/ML time-series or probabilistic models) to represent typical and individualized throwing patterns and predict outcome sensitivity to biomechanical changes.
Generate personalized feedback and training prescriptions by comparing an athlete's model to ideal/clustered motion templates and identifying high-impact corrective targets.
impact: This work shows how pose estimation + interpretable biomechanical features can enable personalized sports coaching and targeted interventions, offering a blueprint for ML practitioners to combine motion capture, feature engineering, and predictive modeling in precision training applications.
visual_elements: Skeleton overlay on a player photo with annotated joint angles and the release point
Timeline / waveform of joint angle trajectories highlighting coordination and release timing
Feature-importance or sensitivity heatmap showing which joints/timings most affect accuracy
Player profile card (radar or bar chart) comparing individual metrics to an optimal/cluster template with suggested drills
paper_title: Toward Personalized Darts Training: A Data-Driven Framework Based on Skeleton-Based Biomechanical Analysis and Motion Modeling
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Dongyi He, Jin Fang, Xi Chen, Yisuo Liu
